en: The Glorious Hymn to Śrī Dakṣiṇāmūrti

I behold the compassionate one who dwells on the slope of the banyan tree— whose lovely lotus-face is radiant with a gentle smile, whose divine form is more beautiful than hundreds of millions of gods of love, and upon whom crescents of moonlight are formed by his soft, copper-hued matted locks.
He is the blossoming seal of awakened consciousness, awakened by the realization of the bliss of absolute liberation.
I meditate upon a certain Rudra, who is like an ocean filled to the brim with the essence of compassion. 2.
Oṃ! Victory, O God, O Great God; victory, O embodiment of compassion!
Victory, O dweller in the forest; victory, O you who sit in the heroic posture! 3.
Victory to you, O Lord of the Daughter of Aṅga, whose body is as white as jasmine, the moon, and sandalwood!
Victory to you, whose hands are gracefully occupied with the gesture of knowledge (*jñānamudrā*), a rosary, and a lute!
Victory to you, who holds a book in another hand, thereby dispelling passion and ignorance!
Victory to you, O Jayāpasmāra, who have placed your right lotus-foot [upon him]!
Victory to you, whose waist shines with the sole garment of a tiger-skin!
Victory to you, whose form is radiant with a noble moon-like face graced by a gentle smile! 5–6.
Victory to you, O slow-moving one, surrounded by a multitude of female disciples!
Victory to you, who have conquered the bodiless god of love through your divine play! Victory to you, the embodiment of auspiciousness!
7 Victory to you, whose chest is lofty and broad! Victory to you, who are fond of music!
Victory to you, O Lord who holds the Gaṅgā; victory to you, O crest-jewel of erotic grace!
Victory to you, O Noble One who clings to the lap [of Pārvatī]; victory to you, O lofty abode upon the mountain!
Victory to you, O Beloved of the gods, who utterly consumed the three cities with a single sidelong glance!
Victory to you, O one with tawny matted locks, who holds the moon in your hand!
Victory to you, the supreme one, skilled at shattering the suffering of those who have sought refuge!
Victory to you, the moon that causes the blue lotuses of knowledge to bloom, the source of both the transcendent and the immanent!
Victory to you, the sun shining forth to destroy the blinding darkness of ignorance!
Victory to you, the destroyer of the demons, who wields the axe for the wilderness of worldly existence! Victory to you, the savior from the ocean of saṃsāra, for those scorched by its heat! 11–12.
Victory to you, the life-restoring medicine for those bitten by the poison of the faults of worldly existence!
Victory to you, the ocean of nectar for those whose inner selves are consumed by the forest fire of their duties!
Victory to you, the navigator who ferries across the people submerged in the ocean of envy!
Victory to you, O Ahata-akshi, the collyrium for the eyes of the world that brings happiness to all beings!
(14) Victory to you, who cuts through the root and the garland of the poisonous creepers of hope! Victory to you, the fiercely blazing fire for the heaps of the grass of sin! (15)
Victory to you, O Supreme Deer who rends the elephant of pride born of illusion!
Victory to you, the unique moon to the moonstone of the hearts of your devotees!
16 Victory to you, the sun to the cranes of the sages who have renounced all worldly hopes!
Victory, O Cakoraka bird for the lovely moon-face of the daughter of Acala!
Victory, O bird for the lofty mountain-like breasts of the Daughter of the Mountain!
Victory, O bee for the charming lotus-face of the daughter of Himavat! 17–18.
Victory to you, O Kātyāyanī, the moon for the blue lotuses of affectionate hearts!
Victory to you, the radiant orb of the sun in the sky of all hearts!
Victory to you, the sovereign ground for playing upon the lofty palace of the bliss of non-attachment!
Victory to you, O actor eager for the dance upon the stage of the assembly of consciousness!
Victory to you, O sovereign whose play in the ocean of infinite awakening is full of wonder!
Victory to you, O cloud beautifully illuminated within the womb of the stainless intellect!
Victory, O joy, you who are like a cuckoo ever-eager for play in a beautiful garden!
Victory, O arrival, you who are like a noble elephant roaming through the forest!
Victory, O *praṇava*, you who are the foremost of parrots within the jeweled cage!
Victory to you, O ocean of all arts, whose orb is like that of the moon!
Victory to you, the refuge of the supernatural powers such as *aṇimā*, the ground of all merit!
Victory to you, who illuminate the three worlds by the very radiance of your own nature! 23–24.
Victory to You, the cause of the birth and other states of the world, extending as far as the earth!
Victory to You, who are devoid of the fabrication of the entire web of the universe! 25 Victory to You, whose form is truth, knowledge, and bliss, and who are attainable by those liberated souls!
Victory to you, O destroyer of Dakṣa’s sacrifice; victory to you, O bestower of the fruit of liberation!
Victory to you, O subtle one who pervades the universe; victory to you, O witness whose nature is consciousness!
Victory to you, O one who transcends all cosmic cycles; victory to you, O ocean of immeasurable virtues!
Victory to you, O Lord who shatters the mirror of Kandarpa’s beauty!
Victory to you, whose limbs are as white as camphor! Victory to you, the refuge of the fruits of all actions!
Victory to you, whose eyes are intent on crushing the pride of the lotus petals!
Victory to you, whose face extinguishes the pride of the full moon’s beauty!

Victory to you, who possess the great splendor of the autumnal moon raised up by the glory of your smile! Victory to you, who surpass the charm of the crimson hue of the bimba fruit with your lower lip! 29–30.
Victory to you, O Lord of glorious necks that put to shame the splendor of conch shells;
victory to you, whose beautiful lotus feet are made radiant by charming anklets!
Victory to you, who are worshipped by Vaikuṇṭha; victory to you of unimpeded intellect, O Hara! Victory to you, the omniscient Śrīkaṇṭha; victory to you, the treasury of all arts!
Victory to you, O treasury of victory, whose hair is the far-reaching sky!
Victory to you, the object of meditation for the Pāśupatas; victory to you, the liberator from bonds!
Victory to you, the Teacher, the Lord of Gods; victory to you, O Śambhu, who pervades the universe!
Victory to you, O Śarva, Lord of Śivā! Victory to you, O Śaṅkara, the eternal!
Victory to you, who are perfectly realized through the single syllable Om! Victory to you, who are compassionate toward your servants!
Victory to you, whose pair of lotus-feet are meditated upon by Brahmā and the other gods!
Victory to you, Bharga, Bhava, and Sthāṇu! Victory to you who are smeared with ashes! Victory to you, the motionless and profound! Victory to you of incomparable prowess!
Victory to you, O Lord from whom all directions have set; victory to you, who have cast down the circle of enemies!
Victory to you, adorned with the three eyes of the sun, the moon, and fire!
Victory to you, O mirror for the cheeks, in which your radiant earrings are reflected!
Victory to you, who are solely devoted to the punishment of heretical folk!
Victory to you whose good fortune is unimpaired! Victory to you, O beloved of Caṇḍī!
Victory to you, the one beloved of Anantā! Victory to you, praised by peaceful people!
(39) Victory to you, perceivable through the three Vedas! Victory to you, who transcend the triad of bodies!
Victory to you, whose nature is the awakening to the non-differentiation of victory; victory to you, who are permeated by the state of being devoid of victory.
Victory to you, free from duality and faultless; victory to you, the ocean of the bliss of non-duality.
Victory to you, eternally without support; victory to you, partless and beyond qualities.
Victory to you who are beyond action and free from fabrication; victory to you who are stainless and fearless!
Victory to you who are soundless and intangible; victory to you who are formless and pure!
Victory to you who are tasteless and odorless; victory to you who are desireless and immovable!
Victory to You, who transcend the boundaries of the world; victory to You, the motionless ocean!
43 Victory to You, O Acyuta; victory to You, the inconceivable; victory to You, the non-dual; victory to You, the imperishable!
Victory to You, the formless; victory to You, the unthinkable; victory to You, the ungraspable; victory to You, the marvelous! 44
Thus ends this most purifying hymn to the Lord of Teachers, which increases one’s sons, grandsons, longevity, health, and all forms of prosperity;
it is the foundation of all knowledge and the perfect bestower of liberation. 45.
Whoever, having become pure, should recite this, attains all fruits.
By the compassionate glance of the Lord of Dākṣāyaṇī,
the wise man realizes the supreme reality right here in this very life.
Neither by religious acts such as bathing, giving, recitation, fire-offerings, and worship of the gods, nor by all the dharmas defined in the Vedas,
can one realize the Self as non-dual pure consciousness alone, through the two mudrās of wordlessness and thoughtlessness.
And there, Mahādeva declares the measure [of the work] by means of books, serpents, and fires.

Alas! A certain matted-haired ascetic, wearing an elephant hide girdled at his waist and displaying some indescribable joy, while holding a skull-cup, brings about the dissolution of the minds of those who behold him;
he is a cakora for the moon of the Vedas' opening words, and an axe for the thicket of the wickedness of those who bow before him.
O Teacher, I bow with joy in my mind to the noble movement of the Sage’s mind.
Thus ends the Śrī Dakṣiṇāmūrtistotra composed by the venerable Sadāśivabrahmendrasvāmin, the most excellent teacher among the wandering mendicants of the Paramahaṃsa order.
